title: CHARACTER*8 NAME — assignment pads short strings with trailing blanks (not nulls)
sourceContent:
SUBROUTINE GREET(NAME)
C     NAME is fixed-width CHARACTER*8. Assigning a 3-character
C     literal leaves the remaining 5 characters as SPACES (' '),
C     not null bytes. A Java String NAME = "BOB" is 3 characters
C     long; a faithful port has to either pad to 8 or trim on
C     read. Forgetting either side leads to silent length
C     mismatches when NAME is compared with literals.
      IMPLICIT NONE
      CHARACTER*8 NAME
      NAME = 'BOB'
C     NAME is now 'BOB     ' -- 3 chars + 5 spaces.
      END
notes: Fixed-width CHARACTER with blank-padding is a recurring source of port bugs. A direct port to Java String preserves the trailing blanks (which break .equals on a literal 'BOB'); a port that trims silently loses them (which breaks anything that depended on the 8-byte width). The spec must capture the width semantic + the comparison policy.
